facts.did: Forty journeys had passed since Gardenpath last visited Tentacle; half that time was burned in frantic preparation for the First and the other half was rotted by institutional hurdles.
facts.anchor: forty journeys since Gardenpath last visited Tentacle.

facts.did: Announced a hitherto unknown rule that any student doing fieldwork in the galaxy had to score high marks in a tedious seminar devoted to planetsuit engineering, which Gardenpath took as targeting them.
facts.anchor: the Science Division announced a hitherto unknown rule

facts.did: Was sympathetic but shrugged when Gardenpath complained, saying it wouldn't be easy and that Gardenpath could probably teach the class themself.
facts.anchor: Professor Arch was sympathetic, but shrugged

facts.did: Used the seminar to track down Barnloft's specs for a planetsuit modification that would mold the body into an Unnamed, did not share the discovery with the seminar, and got a perfect score on the final exam.
facts.anchor: managed to track down Barnloft’s specs for a planetsuit

facts.did: Modeled their new morphology on the Unnamed they had seen making art, giving the suit a setting that cinched the body into an elongated posture with four arms, two eyes, an extremely limited organ for smell, and a tube for generating vibrations.
facts.anchor: They modeled their new morphology on the Unnamed

facts.did: Scrunched by in the Open Lab with a ridiculously tall pile of books swaying in seven arms; the stack collapsed, and Gardenpath rolled to the rescue, grabbing the chitinous casings and easing the volumes onto the bench.
facts.anchor: Column scrunched by with a ridiculously tall pile of books

facts.did: Advised Gardenpath that the Second requires building on the data submitted for the First, and that targeted data gathering was needed to bring the food webs to life - analyzing what makes them sustainable and what rips them apart.
facts.anchor: You need to do some very targeted data gathering

facts.did: Gave Gardenpath a dirty pink notebook that had belonged to one of Column's own students who did a brilliant analysis of an ancient manuscript by Cinderblock, saying it had been headed for the freebie bin; Column put it in a vent so the notebook plumped back up.
facts.anchor: This belonged to one of my students who did a brilliant
